name: Ludrivet
description:
Ludrivet is a playtest workbench for tabletop game designers. It keeps apart three things that playtest notes usually blur together: what the rules said, what actually happened at the table, and what you concluded afterwards.

RULES

Build a prototype with its goal, seat count, round structure and starting resources. Every rule edition keeps its clauses frozen at the version that was actually played, so an old session can never quietly inherit a newer rule. Change a rule through a structured patch: original value, proposed value, numeric effect, the reason, the evidence from your sessions, and the question you want the next playtest to answer. Review what changed between two editions, derive a new draft, and check the freeze before anyone plays on it.

TABLE

Run the session in a dark, low-distraction layout built for one-handed logging at a real table: large timer, seat shapes, live resource state, and an action preview that shows before, change and after. Log Only records an action without passing the turn; Log & End Turn records it and hands off to the next seat. One main action per turn is enforced, and rule exceptions must be explained rather than silently accepted.

Pause for a rule question, a break or a component issue — with or without stopping the clock. Keep a seat ledger that reconciles recorded values against the source events and asks for a reason whenever they differ. Finish a session as Complete, Stopped Early or Abandoned, with final resource and score values, an explicit tie warning, and a quality note.

TRACE

Every event keeps its real timestamp, seat, action, resource deltas and the clause it referenced. Corrections preserve the original event: change time, action, resource movement, clause or note, review the affected table, replay the downstream values, and save with a stated reason. If you leave the app mid-session, the unknown interval becomes a Gap — you classify it yourself and reconstruct only what you actually know, marked as manually entered.

FINDINGS

Compare several completed sessions across rule editions with matched seats, rounds, components and starting values. Every ratio shows its own numerator and denominator. Per-session medians stay separate from pooled ratios. Excluded sessions list their exclusion reason. Charts and tables are generated from the same numbers, and every figure links back to the source session and event.

Saved comparison snapshots keep original result IDs and session revisions. If a source session is later corrected, you get an update warning instead of a silently rewritten result. Turn an observation into an evidence-linked change proposal, then into a rule draft.

FILES AND BACKUP

Select which sections belong in the PDF evidence report — it is a readable, numbered, multi-page text report, not a screenshot. CSV export keeps original events, corrections and effective results on separate rows. A full backup is a checksum-protected JSON that carries the attachment bytes and is restored through a preview, always as a new independent project.

PRIVACY

No account, no ads, no analytics SDK, no server. Your data stays in the app container and in whatever destination you choose through the system document picker. Microphone, camera, photo library, contacts, location, tracking and notifications are never requested. No data is uploaded.

BUILT FOR

· Designers running their own prototype nights
· Playtest groups that want consistent logs across many weeks
· Small studios keeping a paper trail between rule versions
· Anyone who has ever asked "which version did we actually play that under?"

NOTES

· 2–6 seats per session; solo and blind-test seating are out of scope
· Attachments up to 12 MB each; backup import up to 128 MB
· Backup integrity checking is a checksum, not encryption
· A forced termination can lose input recorded since the last successful checkpoint
· Checkpoints run roughly every five foreground seconds

name: Millis: Delay Calculator
description:
Millis turns the measurements you take in a studio into the numbers your plug-ins ask for.

CONVERT
Type a value and tap the unit it is in. Every other unit fills in at once: milliseconds, seconds, samples, frames, timecode, bars and beats, feet, inches, metres, centimetres, Hz and BPM. Distances are sound travelling through air, and the air temperature can be set in °C or °F. Tap any result to copy it.

NOTE LENGTHS
Type the tempo or tap it in. See how long every note lasts, straight, dotted and triplet, from a whole note to a sixty-fourth, as milliseconds, Hz or samples. Use them for delay times, reverb pre-delay and compressor release.

TWO MICS
Enter how far each mic is from the source. Millis shows how much later the far mic hears it, what to delay the near mic by, and where the first comb-filter dip falls if you leave them unaligned.

DRUM KIT
Measure from the middle of each drum to the overheads (or room mics) and to each close mic, typing the readings just as your tape or laser measure shows them: 3' 4", 3 ft 4 in, 1.2 m. A step-by-step tour shows exactly where to measure from and to. Millis gives the delay for every close mic at once, in milliseconds and samples. Choose whether to line up with the nearer overhead, the farther one or the middle, and see how far the other one is still off.

PROJECTS
Save a session by name and come back to it: your settings, the two-mic distances and the whole drum kit. Rename, copy or delete projects any time.

Made for recording and mixing engineers. Works offline, collects no data, and has no ads.
